routes.description: Establish that Christian fellowship and scientific vocation can remain intact while confidence in evolutionary explanations is limited by unresolved causal mechanisms in major biological transitions, origins, and extrapolations beyond observed change.
routes.successCriteria: Show that accepting observable adaptation and interpretive flexibility does not warrant treating proposed mechanisms for body-plan innovation, origins chemistry, or other large-scale transitions as established when their causal sufficiency remains unresolved.

motionBridge.description: Connect unresolved causal mechanisms in the motion's disputed domains to a principled limit on warranted evolutionary confidence without making origins disagreement a test of Christian faith.

centralBridges.description: Require testable causal accounts rather than appeals to unknown biological laws or compressed transition narratives.
Distinguish observed, mechanistically tractable small-scale change from claims about major anatomical and genomic innovation.
Explain why unresolved chemistry and unsupported transition mechanisms materially bear on claims concerning origins and body plans.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test agency-based interpretations against inheritance, selection, and horizontal-transfer explanations where those alternatives apply.
Ground Christian unity and scientific participation in shared faith while allowing multiple interpretations of disputed scriptural and scientific questions.

routes.description: Establish that Christian faith can accommodate a bounded contemporary evolutionary framework enriched by organismal agency, cognition, reciprocal environmental effects, inheritance, and structural principles, despite unresolved mechanisms and limits concerning origins and human uniqueness.
routes.successCriteria: Show that mechanistic incompleteness does not nullify the general evolutionary framework, while defining its proper boundaries and connecting modern biological concepts and scriptural interpretation to a non-hostile relationship between science and Christian faith.

motionBridge.description: Integrate a bounded evolutionary account with Christian commitments by identifying its biological basis, acknowledged limits, and implications for fellowship and scientific vocation.

centralBridges.description: Establish that living systems exhibit environmentally responsive agency or cognition relevant to a non-purely-blind account of evolutionary change.
Explain how niche construction, natural genetic engineering, inheritance, convergence, or structural constraints expand the mutation-selection picture.
Justify retaining a general evolutionary framework despite unresolved mechanisms while avoiding unsupported claims about specific transitions.
Separate biological evolution from claims about life's origin and uniquely human morality, creativity, or spiritual significance.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Relate accurate inheritance and population change to a permissible reading of scriptural language about reproduction according to kind.
Place scientific disagreement within shared Christian identity and preserve space for dialogue and participation in science.

sections.title: Agency, Cognition, and Genome-Directed Adaptation
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether organismal sensing, memory, anticipation, niche construction, and genome modification materially broaden evolutionary explanation or remain accountable to inheritance-and-selection alternatives.

sections.title: Causal Mechanisms and Confidence in the Evolutionary Framework
sections.rationale: The debate centrally turns on whether unknown laws and incomplete mechanisms can coexist with justified acceptance of a general framework, or whether they make broad evolutionary narratives exceed their causal support.

sections.title: Body Plans, Genome Duplication, and Extrapolation Across Scale
sections.rationale: Major anatomical innovation provides the principal test of whether mechanisms associated with mutation, inheritance, and genome duplication can bridge the gap between observed small changes and large evolutionary transitions.

sections.title: Origins, Human Uniqueness, and the Limits of Evolution's Domain
sections.rationale: The proper scope of evolutionary explanation depends on separating biological diversification from the origin of life and from disputed genetic accounts of morality, creativity, behavior, and distinctively human qualities.

sections.title: Scriptural Interpretation, Christian Fellowship, and Scientific Vocation
sections.rationale: Reconciliation also requires an account of how Christians may interpret difficult texts, disagree about origins without salvific division, and participate in science while maintaining shared religious commitments.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Disagreement over evolution should not divide Christians, because scientific disputes can be pursued respectfully while Christians remain united by the truth of Jesus.
moves.attributionBasis: The extended first-person discussion follows Garte's invitation to speak and is answered by Tour at event 212.

response.rationale: This constructive move supplies a supporting theological norm for Christian unity amid scientific disagreement; it has no earlier opposing target to answer.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly advances its assigned unity proposition, though the supporting theological bridge is brief.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim concerns Christian division over scientific disputes, and its scope and unity ground are expressly identifiable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The normative confidence is matched to the stated shared-Christian premise, while scientific uncertainty is expressly acknowledged.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Shared commitment to Jesus coherently supports non-division, with only a bounded implicit bridge from unity to tolerance.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The scientific-dispute analogy and shared-faith premise support the norm, but the theological warrant remains compressed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the subsidiary Christian-unity bridge and sits high within that burden tier.

representationalCharity.rationale: The passage advances a unity norm without engaging a developed contrary interpretation requiring a charity test.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte analogizes respectful scientific disagreement to disputes within faith and expressly grounds continuing unity in the truth of Jesus.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Experiments with bacteria support the claim that living organisms exhibit agency, purpose, environmental sensing, memory, and cognition.
moves.attributionBasis: Tour's request ends at event 280, after which Garte gives a sustained explanation before Tour's confirming question at event 330.

response.rationale: This constructive move introduces experimental work as the basis for organismal agency, purpose, sensing, memory, and cognition; no reply target applies.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it directly advances a central bridge, although the experimental documentation is only summarized.

precisionFindings.rationale: The experimental claim is recoverable, but agency, purpose, and cognition are grouped without fully distinguishing operational meanings.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Invoking a decade of experiments supports confidence, but the broad cognitive vocabulary exceeds the detail supplied in the excerpt.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Experimental behavior can support agency-like capacities, but the bridge from behavior to purpose and cognition remains material.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: A decade of bacterial experiments is invoked, yet protocols, representative results, and operational definitions are not supplied.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly supplies the experimental foundation for the central agency-and-cognition bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move presents positive experimental claims without yet addressing a developed rival account or opposing interpretation.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte expressly says the claims are experimental rather than merely philosophical and attributes them to at least a decade of bacterial work.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Bacteria can learn a recurring temperature-and-oxygen sequence and alter their metabolism before the anticipated oxygen decline occurs.
moves.attributionBasis: Garte begins an explicitly signaled bacterial example and completes it immediately before Tour proposes a possible mechanism.

response.rationale: This constructive example supplies a concrete behavioral sequence intended to demonstrate anticipatory learning in bacteria; it has no earlier opposing target.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, the example gives concrete observable behavior closely connected to the central agency claim.

precisionFindings.rationale: The recurring environmental sequence and metabolic response are recoverable, though the inferential qualification on learning remains implicit.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The described sequence plausibly supports anticipation, but rival selection or transfer mechanisms are not yet excluded.

logicalCoherence.rationale: A conditioned early metabolic response coherently supports anticipation, with one bounded bridge from response timing to learning.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The example describes a relevant experiment, but omits organism identity, protocol detail, controls, and rival-mechanism testing.

relevanceBurden.rationale: This is a concrete and highly relevant supporting instance for the central agency-and-cognition bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: The constructive example precedes the explicit rival mechanism and therefore does not itself perform a charity test.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte describes bacteria exposed to a recurring temperature and oxygen sequence and says their metabolism changes before oxygen falls.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Horizontal DNA transfer and differential bacterial success could explain an apparent community-wide adaptive response without requiring cognition-like anticipation.
moves.attributionBasis: Tour frames the passage as a direct mechanistic question, and Garte answers the proposed hypothesis at the next event.

components.text: Whether the reported community-wide early response requires anticipatory learning rather than an ordinary population-genetic mechanism.
Whether bacterial experimental behavior establishes cognition or purpose rather than adaptive sorting and DNA exchange.

response.rationale: Tour contacts the decisive inference by proposing differential success plus horizontal transfer as a rival explanation, but asks rather than demonstrates that it fits the reported timing and controls.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it reaches the decisive cognition inference but does not verify that the proposed mechanism explains the experiment.

precisionFindings.rationale: The rival mechanism is stated conditionally and its community-level scope is clear and stable.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The proposed explanation is framed as a hypothesis rather than an established diagnosis, matching the limited warrant supplied.

charity.alternative: The bacteria may exhibit learned anticipation expressed before the oxygen decline.
charity.decisiveQualification: Horizontal transfer must explain the response timing and experimental controls, not merely eventual community adaptation.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Differential success followed by DNA transfer is a coherent alternative, conditional on matching the experimental timescale and design.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The mechanism is biologically specific but speculative here; no evidence shows it occurred in the cited experiment.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The reply directly attacks the central inference from bacterial behavior to cognition-like agency.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply offers a serious ordinary-mechanism alternative without denying the observation, though it does not address the crucial timing qualification.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour proposes that a bacterium predisposed to the conditions could outperform neighbors and spread its DNA horizontally through the community.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Evolution does not explain life's origin or exhaustively define human beings, whose distinctive characteristics cannot be reduced to evolutionary products.
moves.attributionBasis: Garte explicitly qualifies Tour's characterization of his position and continues until Tour voices the standard biological response.

components.text: Whether horizontal DNA transfer and differential success explain the bacterial observations without cognition-like anticipation.

response.rationale: The move defines limits on evolution's domain but does not address the earlier horizontal-transfer hypothesis or its challenge to bacterial cognition.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within nonanswers, the material is substantive elsewhere in the debate but does not contact the available opposing demand.

precisionFindings.rationale: The exclusions of life's origin and exhaustive definitions of humanity are expressly stated and scoped.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The domain-boundary claim is firm but bounded, expressly distinguishing biological evolution from origin and human-totalization claims.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between evolution, life's origin, and an exhaustive human account is internally coherent and explicitly bounded.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The scope distinction is defensible, but the claim that some human qualities cannot be evolutionarily explained is asserted here.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly establishes the central bounded-domain bridge and defines two major exclusions.

representationalCharity.rationale: The passage clarifies Garte's own bounded position without evaluating a developed alternative account.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte expressly excludes the origin of life and a complete definition of human beings from evolution's explanatory domain.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Evolutionary explanations of morality, behavior, art, and human uniqueness lack demonstrated genetic mechanisms and often remain unsupported narratives.
moves.attributionBasis: Garte begins by affirming the just-so-story criticism, develops the genetic objection, and concludes with an explicit creationist claim about humanity.

components.text: Whether horizontal transfer and differential bacterial success defeat the inference to cognition-like anticipation.

response.rationale: The move criticizes genetic narratives about human behavior but does not address the only legal earlier opposing move concerning bacterial horizontal transfer.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within nonanswers, it is important to another section but makes no contact with the available earlier opposing component.

precisionFindings.rationale: The criticism is recoverable, but it shifts among morality, kindness, art, behavior, and uniqueness without specifying the evidentiary claim for each.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The absence of identified simple genes supports skepticism, but not the broader implication that evolutionary contributions lack genetic mechanisms altogether.

charity.alternative: Complex human traits may be polygenic and culturally mediated rather than controlled by single trait-specific genes.
charity.decisiveQualification: A lack of simple genes does not itself exclude heritable influences or gene-culture evolutionary accounts.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The argument usefully challenges simple genetic stories, but risks inferring no evolutionary mechanism from no single identified gene.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The oxytocin-receptor example and disease contrast are relevant, yet the broad conclusion lacks representative literature comparison.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the bounded-domain bridge by limiting genetic accounts of distinctively human traits.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move fairly attacks simplistic gene stories but materially underdevelops the strongest polygenic and gene-culture alternative.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte contrasts rare single-gene behavioral disorders with complex ordinary traits and says proposed genes for kindness or love have not been demonstrated.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Invoking unknown biological laws for repeatedly arising features does not supply the specified, testable causal account needed to warrant confidence in the evolutionary explanation.
moves.attributionBasis: The host directly challenges the book's explanatory language from his chemistry-centered perspective.

components.text: Whether evolutionary stories about morality, behavior, art, and human uniqueness lack demonstrated genetic mechanisms.
Whether experimental bacterial behavior establishes agency, purpose, memory, and cognition.
Whether the metabolic response before oxygen decline demonstrates learned anticipation.
Whether evolution excludes life's origin and an exhaustive account of human distinctiveness.

response.rationale: The causal-account objection is highly relevant to the wider mechanism dispute but does not answer the decisive claims of the earlier opposing moves exposed as legal targets.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within relevant nonanswers, it raises a central contrary standard without contacting the selected earlier propositions.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between naming unknown laws and supplying a specified causal account is clear and consistently scoped.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The demand for a specified, testable account is appropriately forceful because an unspecified law does not itself explain the causal pathway.

charity.alternative: Repeated convergence may be evidence that undiscovered structural laws constrain biological outcomes.
charity.decisiveQualification: Evidence for an unknown constraint is not yet a specified causal mechanism for each convergent feature.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The inference cleanly distinguishes evidence suggesting further laws from an actual causal explanation of the observed structures.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The quoted book claim specifically grounds the objection, though the passage does not compare candidate structural mechanisms.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the central requirement for testable causal accounts and sits at the top of that tier.

representationalCharity.rationale: The challenge preserves convergence as a clue while accurately insisting that the clue cannot substitute for the missing causal account.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour quotes the appeal to unknown laws for independently recurring eyes, wings, and social behavior and identifies the missing causal account.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Repeated independent convergence on complex structures indicates nonrandom structural principles beyond mutation and selection, even though those principles remain unknown.
moves.attributionBasis: The guest answers the book-specific challenge by developing the convergence argument and identifying its theoretical implications.

components.text: Whether invoking unknown laws supplies more than a label and yields the specified causal account demanded by Tour.

response.rationale: Garte answers by treating repeated convergence as evidence of additional structural principles and a research clue, but concedes that the principles remain unknown and therefore only partially meets the causal demand.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the decisive inference and clarifies the evidential role of unknown laws, but supplies no mechanism.

precisionFindings.rationale: The convergence claim is recoverable, but structural principles, laws, and nonrandomness are not operationally distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The repeated patterns warrant searching for constraints, but do not by themselves establish that mutation and selection cannot contribute sufficiently.

charity.alternative: Convergent eyes and wings may arise through selection acting on shared constraints without requiring a new category of law.
charity.decisiveQualification: Repeated convergence is evidence of constrained outcomes, but its independence from ordinary evolutionary mechanisms must be shown.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Convergence coherently motivates structural constraints, but the inference to mechanisms beyond mutation and selection remains materially compressed.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Multiple convergent examples are invoked, but their independence, comparability, and inability to arise under existing mechanisms are not demonstrated.

relevanceBurden.rationale: The move directly supports the central expanded-mechanisms bridge through convergence and proposed structural constraints.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply acknowledges ignorance and treats convergence as a clue, yet weakens the rival by saying mutation and selection will not explain it.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte cites independent recurrence of complex eyes, wings, and many other features as clues to unknown constraints beyond a simple mutation-selection picture.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Whole-genome duplication alone does not explain the extensive chemical and anatomical changes required for an invertebrate-to-vertebrate body-plan transition.
moves.attributionBasis: The host cites another passage from the guest's book and frames a direct mechanism-focused objection in his own disciplinary terms.

components.text: Whether repeated convergence establishes structural principles beyond mutation and selection despite their remaining unknown.

response.rationale: The body-plan objection raises the same general demand for mechanism but addresses genome duplication rather than the convergence inference in the legal earlier target.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within relevant nonanswers, it presses a central causal concern but does not answer the earlier convergence argument.

precisionFindings.rationale: The challenged transition, proposed mechanism, and required chemical and anatomical changes are clearly identified.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The passage appropriately claims that duplication alone is incomplete, not that no evolutionary pathway could ever be supplied.

charity.alternative: Genome duplication can provide redundant genetic material later modified through multiple evolutionary processes.
charity.decisiveQualification: That general potential does not specify the steps producing a vertebrate body plan from an invertebrate ancestor.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The fact of duplication does not entail a new body plan, and the demand for intervening steps follows coherently.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The quoted transition supplies a concrete target, but the magnitude claim is not supported with detailed developmental or genomic evidence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly advances the central origins-and-body-plans burden by identifying a specific mechanistic gap.

representationalCharity.rationale: The objection allows that duplication occurred while accurately isolates the missing pathway from redundancy to anatomical innovation.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour quotes the proposed whole-genome-duplication transition and asks how the extensive chemistry needed for a vertebrate body plan is produced.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Major biological mechanisms remain unresolved, but those gaps do not negate the general evolutionary framework, which remains intelligible across many circumstances.
moves.attributionBasis: The guest directly reformulates the host's criticism, acknowledges biological uncertainty, and explains why he nevertheless accepts evolution.

components.text: Whether unresolved chemistry and anatomy in the duplication narrative undermine acceptance of the general evolutionary framework.
Whether acknowledging unknown mechanisms can still warrant confidence in a general evolutionary framework.

response.rationale: Garte explicitly concedes missing mechanisms and answers their claimed consequence by separating incomplete details from the general framework, but gives only a compressed positive warrant for why the framework still holds.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it contacts the decisive consequence of the objections but does not supply the requested transition mechanism.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction is clear, but general idea and most circumstances remain insufficiently specified for exact scope assessment.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Explicit concessions appropriately limit the claim, though saying the framework makes sense in most circumstances is only lightly warranted here.

charity.alternative: A general framework may lose warrant if its central large-scale transitions lack causal mechanisms.
charity.decisiveQualification: Mechanistic gaps do not automatically negate all framework-level evidence, but the independent positive evidence must be identified.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Framework acceptance can coexist with incomplete detail, but the bridge from making sense generally to warranted confidence remains material.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The move rests largely on the assertion that evolution makes sense in most circumstances without representative supporting evidence.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supplies the central framework-under-uncertainty position at the highest relevance within its tier.

representationalCharity.rationale: The response fairly concedes the gaps and rejects automatic negation, but omits the decisive positive evidentiary basis for retention.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte acknowledges unresolved details and mechanisms while distinguishing those gaps from his acceptance of evolution's general idea across many circumstances.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Laboratory-observed microevolution cannot simply be extrapolated to major body-plan innovation because the small changes are mechanistically explainable while the larger transition is not.
moves.attributionBasis: The host contrasts laboratory observations with macroevolutionary body-plan change and issues a direct demand for a stepwise explanation.

components.text: Whether framework-level acceptance remains warranted when major body-plan mechanisms are not explained.
Whether unknown structural principles help explain repeated major biological outcomes.

response.rationale: Tour contacts the framework claim by identifying an asserted failure of extrapolation from explainable small changes to unexplained body-plan innovation, though he does not address all independent support for the framework.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it reaches the decisive warrant issue but challenges only the micro-to-macro extrapolation component.

precisionFindings.rationale: Microevolution, body-plan change, and the claimed mechanistic contrast are clearly and consistently distinguished.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The claim is limited to denying simple extrapolation, and the demand for a stepwise mechanism matches that conclusion.

charity.alternative: Large changes can accumulate through the same population processes operating over longer periods.
charity.decisiveQualification: Shared population processes do not alone demonstrate causal sufficiency for developmental body-plan innovation.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between observed tractable changes and unexplained anatomical innovation directly identifies the missing extrapolative bridge.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: Laboratory microevolution supplies a useful contrast, but no detailed body-plan case or systematic failure analysis is provided here.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly and strongly supports the indispensable central scale-distinction bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: The reply states the strongest scale-continuity alternative and isolates the missing sufficiency bridge without denying small-scale evolution.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour accepts explainable laboratory microevolution but denies that enlarging its scale supplies a mechanism for an invertebrate-to-vertebrate body-plan transition.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Published evidence does not establish that whole-genome duplication produces the large-scale mutational event assumed to underlie vertebrate body-plan innovation.
moves.attributionBasis: The guest recounts personally checking the relevant literature and explicitly concedes the precise genome-duplication point under discussion.

components.text: Whether evidence supplies the large-scale genomic mechanism needed to bridge observed small change and vertebrate body-plan innovation.
Whether whole-genome duplication has been shown to generate the large-scale mutational event assumed in the body-plan narrative.

response.rationale: Garte directly concedes the central evidentiary criticism after checking papers, but does not provide an alternative mechanism for the body-plan transition.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within partial answers, it squarely contacts and concedes the decisive evidence gap, while leaving the broader transition unresolved.

precisionFindings.rationale: The claim is carefully limited to what published evidence has not shown about duplication and large-scale mutation.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The force matches the reported literature check and is limited to non-demonstration rather than impossibility.

charity.alternative: Whole-genome duplication may contribute indirectly through later divergence rather than itself causing one large mutation event.
charity.decisiveQualification: That indirect role does not establish the compressed duplication-to-body-plan mechanism under challenge.

logicalCoherence.rationale: If the literature does not show the assumed large event, the compressed evidentiary bridge is legitimately undermined.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The reported inspection of ten papers is specific and adverse to prior belief, though search method and representativeness remain bounded gaps.

relevanceBurden.rationale: By conceding the missing large-scale evidence, it directly attacks the central pro scale-distinction burden.

representationalCharity.rationale: The concession accurately addresses the evidentiary limitation without claiming duplication is biologically irrelevant or impossible.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte reports that the first ten papers he inspected said whole-genome duplication had not been shown to cause a large-scale mutation event.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Loss of a proposed prebiotic route to sugars is a major origin-of-life setback because ribose and related sugars are required for pathways toward RNA and DNA.
moves.attributionBasis: The host draws a general lesson from the preceding concession and then applies it to a specific origin-of-life chemistry example.

components.text: Whether excluding life's origin from evolution adequately bounds the evolutionary framework and reconciliation claim.
Whether a general evolutionary framework remains warranted despite unresolved mechanisms.
Whether the genome-duplication literature fails to establish a large mutational event.

response.rationale: The chemistry example is relevant to origins but does not contest Garte's express exclusion of life's origin from evolution, nor answer the other legal earlier claims.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within relevant nonanswers, it provides important contrary origins material but leaves the earlier bounded-domain claim intact.

precisionFindings.rationale: The pathway and required sugars are identifiable, but no more route risks shifting from loss of one route to loss of all routes.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Loss of a major route can be a serious setback, but the excerpt does not warrant certainty that no prebiotic sugar route remains.

charity.alternative: Refutation of one proposed synthesis pathway need not eliminate all possible routes to prebiotic sugars.
charity.decisiveQualification: If that route carried the principal experimental burden, its failure still materially weakens current origin scenarios.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Sugars are required for RNA and DNA, but the inference from one failed synthesis to no route is insufficiently supported.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: A specific reaction failure is invoked, yet neither the paper nor the exclusivity of that pathway is established in the passage.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the central origins-and-body-plans burden through a specific origin-chemistry limitation.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move identifies the pathway's importance but rhetorically collapses one route's failure into the absence of every route.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour says a proposed sugar-synthesis reaction failed and argues that losing access to ribose and related sugars blocks RNA and DNA pathways.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: Disagreement about earth history or evolution is not a salvific heresy, and serious commitment to scripture permits differing interpretations of difficult passages.
moves.attributionBasis: The host affirms the guest's unity theme and supports it with an explicit theological argument about salvation and scriptural interpretation.

components.text: Whether disagreement over evolution should remain non-divisive within shared Christian commitment.

response.rationale: Tour directly affirms the unity claim and adds a theological reason: positions on earth history and evolution are not conditions of salvation, while difficult texts permit disagreement.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within full answers, it explicitly contacts the decisive non-division claim and supplies an independent salvific qualification.

precisionFindings.rationale: The distinction between scriptural seriousness, interpretive disagreement, heresy, and salvation is expressly maintained.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The categorical rejection of a salvific test is tied to an explicit theological criterion and does not overclaim scientific truth.

charity.alternative: Some Christians regard a particular origins interpretation as required by scriptural faithfulness.
charity.decisiveQualification: Scriptural importance does not make an interpretation a condition of salvation absent a salvific textual basis.

logicalCoherence.rationale: The distinction between important interpretation and salvific doctrine is explicit and supports the non-division conclusion.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The theological criterion and acknowledged interpretive difficulty provide strong support, though detailed exegesis is compressed.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly and strongly supports the subsidiary pro faith-pluralism bridge.

representationalCharity.rationale: Tour recognizes serious scriptural commitment while accurately separates interpretive disagreement from salvation and heresy.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour rejects claims that origins disagreement is heresy or forfeits salvation and affirms differing interpretations among people committed to scripture.

moves.speaker: Sy Garte
moves.proposition: Accurate inheritance is indispensable to evolution, and Genesis language about creatures reproducing according to kind is consistent with population-level evolutionary biology.
moves.attributionBasis: The surrounding exchange and first-person reference to a previously discussed chapter identify Garte as the speaker presenting his book's inheritance argument.

response.rationale: This constructive move connects accurate inheritance, population continuity, and Genesis language about reproduction according to kind; no reply target applies.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it clearly builds the scriptural-compatibility bridge, though the population-level interpretive warrant is compressed.

precisionFindings.rationale: Inheritance and according to kind are stable terms, while the exact interpretive bridge to population evolution is implicit.

calibrationFindings.rationale: Accurate inheritance is appropriately presented as necessary for evolution, while compatibility with Genesis is a bounded interpretive claim.

charity.alternative: According to kind may be read as restricting change beyond fixed created categories.
charity.decisiveQualification: The phrase also describes reliable reproduction, which is necessary for population descent and does not itself specify immutable boundaries.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Reliable inheritance coherently connects reproduction according to kind with evolutionary population continuity, with one interpretive bridge implicit.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The biological necessity of inheritance is well grounded, but the scriptural compatibility claim receives only abbreviated textual support.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the subsidiary scriptural-compatibility bridge and is highly placed within that tier.

representationalCharity.rationale: The move offers a fair compatibility reading but does not fully engage the strongest fixed-category textual interpretation.

moves.evidenceBasis: Garte identifies accurate inheritance as indispensable to evolution and links it to Genesis's repeated description of reproduction according to kind.

moves.speaker: James Tour
moves.proposition: More Christians should enter science so later generations can see that devotion to Jesus is compatible with doing good scientific work.
moves.attributionBasis: The alternating closing exchange attributes the initial appeal and its concluding formulation to Tour, with Garte briefly affirming between those portions.

response.rationale: This constructive closing move supports Christian scientific participation by asserting the compatibility of devotion to Jesus and good scientific work; no target applies.

responsivenessWithinClass.rationale: Within constructive moves, it directly advances faith pluralism and vocation, although it is a brief exhortation rather than an argument.

precisionFindings.rationale: The vocational appeal and compatibility claim are concise, fully recoverable, and require no material scope qualification.

calibrationFindings.rationale: The exhortative force is proportionate to the compatibility claim and does not make a disputed empirical assertion.

logicalCoherence.rationale: Encouraging Christian participation coherently follows from the asserted compatibility of faith and competent science.

evidenceWarrant.rationale: The compatibility claim is plausible within the exchange, but this short closing move supplies little independent support.

relevanceBurden.rationale: It directly supports the subsidiary faith-pluralism and scientific-vocation burden.

representationalCharity.rationale: The closing exhortation does not engage a live contrary interpretation requiring a charity assessment.

moves.evidenceBasis: Tour calls for more Christians in science so future generations can see that loving Jesus is compatible with doing good science.
